html:
The Santee, or Isanti, are the eastern division of the Dakota, the Sioux peoples of Minnesota. They include four bands: the Mdewakanton, Wahpekute, Wahpeton and Sisseton. Their homeland lay around the upper Mississippi and the Minnesota River.

They lived by hunting deer and bison, fishing, gathering wild rice and making maple sugar, and grew some maize. In the 1700s pressure from the Ojibwe, armed through the French fur trade, pushed them south and west out of the northern lake country, while relatives such as the Yankton and Lakota moved further onto the plains.

Treaties in 1851 took most of their land and confined them to a strip along the Minnesota River. When promised payments failed and families went hungry, some Dakota went to war in 1862, in the Dakota War of 1862. After it, 38 Dakota men were hanged at Mankato, the largest mass execution in United States history, and most Santee were expelled from Minnesota. Many now live on the Santee Sioux reservation in Nebraska and in Dakota communities in the Dakotas, Minnesota and Canada. Early neighbours in Minnesota included the Cheyenne and Iowa.
